title: The Formulary
corpus_scope: ICLR 2026 · 293,671 negative units, embedded locally · nearest twin always from a different paper
question: Which criticisms are field-wide formulas repeated across papers, and which are written for the paper at hand — and does that distinction change what the objection costs?

figures.title: The spectrum: how close is your criticism's nearest twin?
figures.deck: Most criticisms have a familiar twin in someone else's review — the median criticism's nearest twin sits at 0.81 similarity.

claims.statement: The median criticism's nearest twin sits at 0.81 similarity.
claims.derivation: median nearest-other-paper-twin cosine similarity across all 293,671 embedded 2026 negative units
share of the 293,671 embedded 2026 negative units whose nearest-twin similarity clears the 0.85 threshold

claims.statement: 3.8% are formulas with a twin above 0.90.
claims.derivation: share of the 293,671 embedded 2026 negative units whose nearest-twin similarity clears the 0.90 threshold, the cutoff behind every formula share on this plate

figures.title: Formula share by object, against what the objection costs in score
figures.deck: The objections that cost the most score are the hand-written ones (novelty: 1.3% formula share); the cheap ones are standard formulas (reproducibility: 8.7%).

claims.statement: The objections that cost points are the paper-specific ones — novelty at 1.3% and framing at 1.2% formula share, method and theory at 1.5%.
claims.derivation: per-object share of negative units whose nearest twin clears 0.90 (by_object[o].shares[1]) for novelty, problem_framing, method_design, theory, joined against Plate XIV's within-paper tariff coefficient for the same objects

claims.statement: The free objections are the formulaic ones: reproducibility 8.7%, clarity 8.0%.
claims.derivation: per-object share of negative units whose nearest twin clears 0.90 (by_object[o].shares[1]) for reproducibility and clarity, joined against Plate XIV's within-paper tariff coefficient for the same objects

caveats.text: What is compared is the model's tidied restatement of each criticism, not the reviewer's raw sentence, and that tidying pulls different phrasings closer together — so read the absolute similarity levels as upper bounds, and trust the comparisons (like the rise with score), which all pass through the same instrument.
The tariff pole of Fig. 10b is borrowed from Plate XIV's within-paper 2026 regression and carries that plate's caveats (bootstrap intervals, single-year scope, association not causation).
